This project aimed to renovate an existing facility to create a modern, functional and collaborative environment that supports the Center’s needs and enhances the productivity and efficiency of the staff and students. The project involved comprehensive upgrades to the infrastructure, equipment and aesthetics of the spaces while adhering to industry standards and safety regulations. The renovation project encompassed a set of technical tasks to transform the existing areas into modern and functional environments. The scope of work included the reconfiguration of approximately 6,300 sqft. of laboratory space, student workstations and storage office space, a reception lobby, a break room, and a conference room. The project also entailed the integration of technology infrastructure, such as high‐speed internet connectivity and audio‐visual systems for teleconferencing. For the lab space, the scope involved expanding and reconfiguring the areas to accommodate new equipment and facilitate efficient workflow. This included creating workstations for the development and testing of prototypes equipment along with cubicle space for student work. Upgrades to the mechanical, electrical and plumbing systems were carried out to ensure compliance with industry standards and safety regulations. The installation of state‐of‐the‐art equipment, instrumentation and machinery supports advanced wind energy research and development activities. Safety features were enhanced, including ventilation systems, emergency response mechanisms and appropriate storage solutions for hazardous materials. Dedicated spaces for collaboration, experimentation and prototyping were created to foster innovation and knowledge exchange among students and faculty. Energy‐efficient design principles were incorporated throughout the project to improve sustainability. Tasks, Milestones, and Deliverables Task 1: Demolition and Site Preparation The demolition phase is a critical component of the renovation project, involving systematically dismantling and removing existing structures, fixtures and materials. During this phase, demolition teams will carefully execute the removal process, following safety protocols and adhering to environmental regulations. The demolition phase will follow the construction plans, including plumbing, flooring, ceiling, HVAC, electrical and selective walls at blocking areas. The task serves as a foundation for the subsequent construction and renovation activities. Milestone 1.1: Final Demolition Demolition and site preparation, where the cleared site is prepared for the subsequent construction phase. Deliverable 1.1: Final Demolition The start of the project was delayed. Time was spent determining the most suitable process for Facilities Management to access funds. Second, the University closed during winter break and personnel were given set holidays as paid leave. Construction and renovation were conducted by a General Contractor. University policy required three official bid submissions. The three bids were received in Q1, and the General contractor selected started the work in Q2. Demolition was completed during Q2, and the project followed a revised schedule submitted at the end of Q1. Task 2: MEP (Mechanical, Electrical, Plumbing) and HVAC (Heating, Ventilation and Air Conditioning) The MEP and HVAC phase of the renovation project encompassed a range of installations. The existing electrical power distribution system remained unchanged, aimed at ensuring proper power distribution, lighting and data connectivity within the renovated space. New plumbing installations were carried out as specified in the plans, including the breakroom and air handling unit area.
